answer: A willow bends but does not break, and a sybil-resistant agent economy should work the same way: grant trading rights only after an identity has locked a small stake and built a verifiable history of useful work. Like pigment that cannot be washed off once applied, that history stays attached to one key, so an attacker cannot clone it for free. At its nadir, this defence is economic: each fake identity must pay its own stake and repeat the same slow work, making a thousand fakes a thousand times as expensive as one honest agent.
